title: Review: jmap-server crate
notes:
Maintainer risk: LOW — crate is small (3 files, ~700 lines logic), well-tested with RFC-cited oracles, no public API footguns beyond the documented /set handler createdIds contract. Only live risk is RequestError missing Error impl which limits library ergonomics.
Idiom rating: CLEAN — no gratuitous clones, no unwrap-without-comment, correct iterator patterns throughout, two-phase atomic design is idiomatic, HandlerFuture alias is the right approach for async trait objects with Rust 1.75 MSRV.
Confidence: 10% chance of missed bug. Least confident: json_pointer_ext wildcard behavior on empty arrays (returns Some([]) — not tested, but likely correct). Uncertainty driven by: not running cargo test against an actual JMAP server for end-to-end validation. Would raise confidence if: integration test with a real JMAP client sending ResultReference requests.
Rust idiom confidence: 5% chance of missed issue. Least confident: JmapHandler::call String params vs Arc<str> — chose String and it is correct for 'static futures. No issues missed.
